prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1101; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at a red light in the left lane of the roadway in Pasadena, Texas, when Driver 2 failed to stop in time and struck the rear of Driver 1's vehicle. The impact pushed Driver 1's car forward into the intersection, and the damage to the rear bumper, trunk lid and tail light assembly is consistent with the force described by both drivers. Driver 2 stated that the light had changed and that the brakes did not respond quickly enough on a wet pavement surface. Two independent witnesses on the adjoining sidewalk gave statements that matched this account, and photographs taken at the scene show the same damage pattern. Officers found no prior damage to the vehicle in any records or observations made at the scene. Passenger was seated in the front right seat and was confirmed present by both drivers and by both witnesses. Passenger reported pain in the left knee after the collision and was evaluated at the scene, where the reported injury was considered plausible given the direction and force of the impact. Driver 1 is listed as a member of the policyholder's household and was operating the vehicle with permission.
